title: Learning to See — Latent Texture & Cluster Traverse
subtitle: Traversing archival water, vapor, cell lattices, and cosmos by visual affinity
lineage: Lineage: Memo Akten, Learning to See (2017) · Supporting: SCION 109 (Soft Cinema), SCION 112 ( Cultural Analytics)
theorem: Traverse an archival database along continuous morphological and textural gradients—rippling water, billowing vapor, spider webs, cellular lattices, and star fields—while keeping the difference between visual similarity and historical origin visible.
boundary_note: Demonstrates database neighborhood traversal (`SCION 109–113`): visual embedding proximity connects water (`545715d8`), vapor (`5a15eff7`), web (`2ab9061b`), and stars (`ed87f1da`) without erasing their provenance.

v1_defect_timecodes: Seg #07 (t=24.90s-29.90s): `ed87f1da` (`The Eclipse`, 1907) at 0.5s-5.5s showed a static intertitle card (`MotionΔ=0.2, Luma=8`).
Seg #08 (t=29.90s-35.90s): `5a15eff7` in Quad defaulted to 0.0s without `custom_window=True`.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: Replaced the static 1907 intertitle in Seg #07 with verified luminous condensing blue vapor nebula (`005ac24d`, `Hot Lava Flows Into The Ocean`, `2.5s-7.5s`, `MotionΔ=44.4`) and enabled `custom_window=True` on `5a15eff7` (`17.2s-21.7s`) in both Seg #03 and Seg #08 Quad.
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Traverse 6 moving textural fields (`545715d8`, `5a15eff7`, `953cc54f`, `2ab9061b`, `efedc39b`, `005ac24d`) and close with a 4-cluster latent neighborhood quad.
